issue-4606: Close button on notifications is read as "Dismiss" in French
Opened by a11y-review-cm on 2026-11-04

One of our accountants uses VoiceOver with her Ledgerline profile set to French.
The text of the small notifications at the bottom of the page is read in French
("Fichier reçu. L'import va bientôt commencer."), but the close button on every
notification is announced as "Dismiss, button". The upload form and the date
range picker around it are read in French too.

input.title: Translate the toast close button's label using the user's locale
input.body:
File: src/components/Toast.tsx

Toast calls t("ui.toast.dismiss") without a locale argument, so t() falls back to DEFAULT_LOCALE ("en") and the close button's aria-label is always "Dismiss", even though fr.json has "Fermer". The other components (DateRangePicker, ReportTable) take an optional locale prop and pass it to t(). Change Toast to accept a locale (default "en") and pass it as the third argument of t(), and have ToastProvider accept the same locale and hand it down to each Toast. The app shell that mounts ToastProvider should then pass the user's locale, as the other components already receive it.

text: The cause is confirmed: `Toast.tsx` never passes the user's locale to `t()`, so the close button always gets the English label. I'll label it a bug and open the pull request.

text:
Issue #4606 is triaged as a bug, with the fix in `src/components/Toast.tsx`.

The close button's accessible label comes from `t("ui.toast.dismiss")`, which is called without a locale. `t()` then falls back to the English default, so the button is always announced as "Dismiss". `fr.json` already has the French string ("Fermer") for that key. The date range picker and table get the locale passed in, which is why they are read in French.

I applied the `bug` label, opened draft pull request pr-17 from `repomind/issue-4606`, and posted the comment. The pull request describes the change in prose and does not commit code. It proposes passing a locale into `Toast` and `ToastProvider`, the same way `DateRangePicker` already does. I did not run the test suite, and I did not check where the app mounts `ToastProvider`, so that wiring is still to be confirmed.
